name: The Explosion
label: Revelation
lede: The Explosion sold 250 demo tapes on a Kid Dynamite tour, landed on Spin's top 20 of 2000, and settled a legal threat with an EP. Then Virgin dropped them, and the album they'd finished for it waited five years.

eras.title: Two hundred and fifty tapes
eras.text: The Explosion came together in Boston in fall 1998 through the Big Wheel Recreation crowd, with a bassist fresh from the straight edge band In My Eyes. A homemade demo and a tour with Kid Dynamite got them a record deal.

years.h: The Explosion forms in Boston, through Big Wheel Recreation
years.p: Matt Hock and Damian Genuardi, fresh from In My Eyes, meet guitarist David Walsh through Rama Mayo of Big Wheel Recreation. Drummer Dan Colby and guitarist Sam Cave, from the band Trouble, join soon after.

years.h: 250 demo tapes go out on tour with Kid Dynamite
years.p: The band presses 250 copies of its demo and sells them on the road. One reaches Jade Tree, which signs the band.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, a roadie delivered the demo to Jade Tree. The label's first Explosion release, the self-titled EP in 2000, collects every song from it.

eras.title: Spin applauds, Revelation threatens
eras.text: Flash Flash Flash landed on Spin's list of the top 20 albums of 2000. Then Revelation Records, which still had Damian Genuardi's old band In My Eyes, threatened to sue him if he was credited on Explosion records.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Explosion · Wikipedia: The Explosion (EP)
years.h: Jade Tree releases the demo as an EP
years.p: The self-titled EP puts six songs from the tour demo on a label with national reach.

years.src: Wikipedia: Flash Flash Flash · Wikipedia: The Explosion
years.h: Flash Flash Flash makes Spin's top 20 of the year
years.p: Fourteen songs in 27 minutes, recorded in February 2000 and opening with No Revolution.
years.xp:
The Washington Post called it "an artifact from the open-nerve period of adolescent development". Robert Christgau gave it a choice-cut mention. The track list includes Reactor, Terrorist and Tarantulas Attack.

Spin later named the band one of 2001's top-10 punk acts, and the Boston Phoenix put them second for best local punk act.

years.src: Wikipedia: Steal This · Wikipedia: The Explosion · Revelation Records
years.h: The band hands Revelation an EP to settle the claim
years.p: Revelation, home of Genuardi's old band In My Eyes, had threatened to sue him if he was credited on Explosion records. Steal This (REV 98) ends it.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Revelation believed The Explosion's success on Jade Tree should have gone to its own label. The band wrote the EP on tour, and Wikipedia notes it isn't considered their best work. It runs 8:57.

Revelation's first pressing: 300 red and 1,975 black copies. In My Eyes' own albums on Revelation were REV 67 (1998) and REV 80 (1999).

years.h: Warped Tour, then years opening for bigger names
years.p: The Explosion play the 2001 Warped Tour and keep touring the US and Europe with [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]], [[Alkaline Trio|69421e11-e4c3-4854-951b-ceab4972e38e]], [[Social Distortion|e1e05cce-3922-44e1-8f20-015abe5e309d]], [[The (International) Noise Conspiracy|97da5eb3-79a5-4195-b98e-3d10ef946b08]] and [[Rocket from the Crypt|e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a]].
years.xp: Wikipedia also lists dates with Sick of It All and Joe Strummer and the Mescaleros.

years.h: Jade Tree's Location Is Everything, Vol. 1 includes the band
years.p: The label's compilation, out April 16, lists The Explosion with the rest of its roster.

eras.title: Virgin signs them, then shelves the second album
eras.text: Seven major labels bid for the band and Virgin won. A second Virgin album, Bury Me Standing, got finished, the label dropped them, and the band called it quits.

years.h: Sick of Modern Art comes out on the band's own Tarantulas label
years.p: Virgin distributes the EP, put out on Tarantulas Records.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, seven major labels were bidding for the band and Virgin got the deal.

years.h: Black Tape puts the band on Virgin
years.p: The major-label debut comes out October 5, with the Red Tape EP on Tarantulas alongside it.
years.xp:
It was recorded at Cider Mountain Recorders. Here I Am reached No. 37 on the US Modern Rock chart and No. 75 on the UK Singles chart. The band played Late Night with Conan O'Brien on October 21, 2004.

Songs turned up in Tony Hawk's Underground, Burnout 3: Takedown and NFL Street 2. The UK release followed on March 15, 2005.

years.h: Virgin pushes Here I Am and No Revolution as singles
years.p: Instant Live releases Live in Boston on June 21, and the band plays a second Warped Tour.
years.xp: No Revolution reached No. 107 on the UK Singles chart in 2005.

years.h: Colby and Cave out, Black and Gonzalez in
years.p: Andrew Black takes the drum stool from Dan Colby, and Chris Gonzalez, formerly of [[Let It Burn|71a59653-b14e-4e6f-9ac5-28472638fd31]], replaces guitarist Sam Cave.

years.h: Virgin drops the band, and Bury Me Standing sits on a shelf
years.p: The second Virgin album is finished and goes unreleased.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, the album was recorded in 2006, and the band announced its departure from Virgin on February 13, 2007.

years.h: The Explosion post the breakup on their website
years.p: A last run of shows is booked.

years.h: The last show, in New York, nine years after Boston
years.p: The Explosion play their final show on September 4, 2007.

eras.title: Bury Me Standing, finally
eras.text: The Explosion came back for short runs, and Bury Me Standing finally came out in 2012. From 2019 they were a working band again, opening for Bad Religion.

years.h: Asbury Park hosts the first show since the split
years.p: The Explosion reunite with the Bouncing Souls at their "Home For The Holidays" event.
years.xp: The date was December 28, 2011. That month the Bouncing Souls' label, Chunksaah Records, announced it would release Bury Me Standing.

years.h: Bury Me Standing comes out on Valentine's Day, five years late
years.p: The album finished for Virgin in early 2007 is finally released.
years.xp: It had been announced for March 2008 on Paper + Plastick Records, which didn't happen. Chunksaah Records, run by the Bouncing Souls, put it out on February 14, 2012.

years.h: Bad Religion brings the band back on the road
years.p: After one-off reunions in 2014 and 2016, The Explosion return as an active band with Black and Gonzalez, supporting [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]].
years.xp:
The 2014 show was This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia, in April; 2016 was Asbury Park, on July 29. Bad Religion announced the Explosion as support on May 8, 2019.

Hock and Walsh also play in Space Cadet, Walsh and Gonzalez in the Loved Ones.
